stories.title: Claude Frontier Academy: $100M to train 10,000 engineers
stories.summary: Claude Frontier Academy trains Frontier Deployed Engineers to the standard of Anthropic’s own — a $100 million commitment to train 10,000 by the end of 2027.

sources.name: Anthropic
sources.title: Claude Frontier Academy: $100M to train 10,000 engineers
sources.text: The first-of-its-kind Academy trains Frontier Deployed Engineers using the same standard of skills as Anthropic’s own engineers, starting with cohorts from Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley, Novo Nordisk and others. Today we are launching Claude Frontier Academy to solve one of the most pressing issues in AI implementation: talent. Backed by a $100 million commitment, Anthropic aims to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers (FDEs) by the end of 2027. Engineers from Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley and Novo Nordisk are in the first cohorts. Every enterprise is racing to bring AI into its organization, but the people with the skills to make it work inside a real business have become the hardest talent to find. Inside the companies we work with, a small group of deeply skilled people drives an outsized share of what AI delivers. The Academy is the first of its kind from an AI company, built from our own work deploying Claude inside the world’s largest enterprises and the professional services organizations that serve them. “A small team of high-agency people with the right skills, access to Claude, and a deep understanding of how their business runs can transform an entire company. The hard part is building that depth of talent, engineers with the highest level of AI fluency who can take Claude from an idea to a system in production and turn it into faster processes and new products and services. No AI company has invested in developing that talent inside its customers and partners at this depth. Claude Frontier Academy trains people the way our own engineers learn, and we want those who graduate to set the standard for how AI gets built inside a business.” – Steve Corfield, Global Head of Business Development and Partnerships at Anthropic The Academy’s first program, the Frontier Deployed Engineer Residency, follows the medical model for building expertise. Doctors learn from practicing physicians, train on real cases, and are assessed before they practice alone. Likewise, FDE Residency engineers learn from practitioners, practice on realistic cases, and are assessed on their work before they earn the credential. The goal is agentic systems that change how a business runs, from faster, redesigned processes to new products and services. The program is for hands-on software engineers with strong fundamentals, a record of building with LLMs, experience helping others adopt AI, and a habit of tackling their business’s most important problems. Organizations nominate their strongest engineers, each arriving with a named Claude project to lead when they return. Prior experience building AI agents isn’t required. Engineers start with a multi-day in-person program with Anthropic engineers and licensed instructors. They work through a simulated enterprise deployment, from the right use case through security review to handover, and finish with a graded practical on a new scenario. Those who pass earn the Claude Resident Engineer badge and move into the 12-week residency, where they lead a real Claude use case at their own organization, supported by Anthropic engineers and learning from their cohort as they build. Engineers are assessed again at the end of the 12 weeks, and those who pass earn the Claude Frontier Deployed Engineer badge, with the first expected in early 2027. Cohorts are running in San Francisco, New York and London. The program will grow toward 10,000 engineers by the end of 2027. Participation is by nomination; organizations can ask their Anthropic account team or Partner Account Manager whether they’re eligible. Claude Frontier Academy builds on the Claude Partner Network , where professionals across 46,000 firms have earned more than 175,000 Claude certifications and nearly 4,000 people have completed Basecamp, an immersive program that teaches the same curriculum our Applied AI teams receive when they onboard. Claude Frontier Academy is for the people who will lead the work, and training 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers is the first step of many. We’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program, which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals. Barclays, the British universal bank, is expanding its strategic collaboration with Anthropic to integrate secure, enterprise-grade AI systems across its global operations. We’re announcing a new life sciences research group and laboratory at Anthropic. This post introduces the team behind this work and shares early results in which Claude discovered a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of CRISPR.

sources.title: Anthropic earmarks $100 million to train over 10,000 AI engineers in push to develop enterprise AI
sources.text: Anthropic wants 10,000 FDEs by 2027, with a twist Anthropic has announced plans to spend a mammoth $100 million to launch its Claude Frontier Academy, a training scheme designed to support enterprise AI adoption. The company is targeting 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers (FDEs) by the end of 2027, who will be able to identify use cases, handle security considerations and drive deployment for Claude customers. "Claude Frontier Academy trains people the way our own engineers learn, and we want those who graduate to set the standard for how AI gets built inside a business," Steve Corfield, Global Head of Business Development and Partnerships at Anthropic explained. The training scheme starts with a simulated enterprise deployment before trainees enter a 12-week residency "where they lead a real Claude use case at their own organization." The initial cohorts are set to include engineers from major consulting and financial organizations, including Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley and Novo Nordisk. Anthropic has already given out more than 175,000 Claude certifications to workers across 46,000 companies part of its broader Claude Partner Network, but the drive behind its latest FDE scheme is clear. The easier it becomes for enterprise customers and consultancies to deploy Claude, the more customers Anthropic is likely to have. Additionally, working with consultancies gives Anthropic access to their customers, extending its reach. Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed! Rival company OpenAI already has its own extensive FDE scheme, too, but there's a key difference. OpenAI's focus is on training its own workers to go off and transform customers' companies, but Anthropic's latest announcement is primarily about training other companies' engineers to become FDEs. Reuters recently reported that OpenAI has experienced a twofold increase in enterprise sales since July 2026, and while specific figures are kept closely under wraps, we do know that enterprise deals are far more lucrative for companies like Anthropic than consumer subscriptions. So while a $100 million commitment to train engineers may sound like a large sum, Anthropic clearly hopes it will pay off in the long run. sources.title: How to watch the Microsoft Windows and Surface event
sources.text: The Microsoft Windows and Surface event will take place in San Francisco later today, beginning at 10AM PT (1PM ET), and there's a lot we expect to see . It's certainly going to be a very AI-focused event. According to Microsoft, it will center on a "conversation on how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC." It will be broadcast live on Microsoft's YouTube channel , and is expected to run for about an hour. To make things convenient, we've also embedded it here in this article below. The event isn't just noteworthy because of its heavy AI focus (though the effort to drum up excitement on the subject is an interesting choice after widespread negative reactions led to the scaling back of Copilot's presence in the OS ). It's also significant as the first laptop-centric event the company has held in two years. Considering NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang is one of the featured speakers alongside Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and head of Windows and Devices Pavan Davuluri, chances are high that we'll see an update about the Surface Laptop Ultra, as the laptop is powered by NVIDIA's RTX Spark superchip . The RTX Spark is all about AI, with NVIDIA claiming it delivers 1 petaflop of AI computing power. This goes hand-in-hand with Microsoft's shifting focus to agentic AI, which is AI that needs minimal input from you to operate. The Surface Laptop Ultra and Spark come together to make an AI powerhouse, the cost of which still remains a mystery, but will likely be revealed during today's event. Whether the concept of an AI-capable MacBook competitor resonates enough with the average consumer to generate sales from said price point is still up in the air. When it comes to whether Windows 12 is on the table, it doesn't look too likely. The company has already gone on record and said a new OS wouldn't be released in 2026. With that being the case, it's unlikely they would take the time to delve into a new system that wouldn't be seen for at least several months. The company also seems more focused on making improvements and tweaks to Windows 11, from visual adjustments and Start menu fixes to a better File Explorer and large-scale AI integration. It also doesn't make much sense to release a brand-new operating system just ahead of launching the Surface Laptop Ultra, since the system and the RTX Spark are designed for Windows 11. Regardless, it won't be long before we see what Microsoft has to show today, and our team will be on the ground covering the news live. Stick around, as we'll be liveblogging the event and writing up our hands-on impressions and analyses of what the company reveals.

sources.title: Microsoft Windows and Surface event 2026: Live updates as Satya Nadella and Jensen Huang take the stage
sources.text: More details on the Surface Laptop Ultra and NVIDIA RTX Spark are coming, but what else? Microsoft is expected to unveil more details about the Surface Laptop Ultra at its Windows and Surface event in San Francisco. The company has also teased "latest innovations across Windows, NVIDIA RTX Spark, Surface and the broader PC ecosystem." In its invitation, Microsoft said we would hear from CEO Satya Nadella and Windows and Devices chief Pavan Davuluri , as well as NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. The presentation, which is scheduled to start at 10AM PT (1PM ET), should last about an hour, and you can watch the company's livestream across its X, Instagram and YouTube channels. Or you could just stay here and follow along on our liveblog. Our senior reporters Karissa Bell and Devindra Hardawar will be on the ground bringing you updates live from the scene. We'll be starting our liveblog in just a couple of hours at 10AM ET, keeping you up to speed on the latest rumors and teases right up to the launch. As you wait, feel free to leave us comments below and we'll be sure to answer them when we can. To recap, we already caught a glimpse of the Surface Laptop Ultra earlier this year at the company's Build developer conference. It's supposed to be the most powerful Surface yet, thanks to the power of NVIDIA's RTX Spark superchip. We know it's got a 15-inch mini LED display that gets up to 2,000 nits bright. It has the largest trackpad Microsoft has ever made, plus a generous offering of ports including USB C, USB A and a full-sized SD card reader onboard. Today, though, we're likely to find out more about pricing, availability and other software features. And if we didn't also learn about some type of Agentic AI capability coming to Windows, I'll be shocked. Still, given the company's recent troubled history with rolling out AI features to Windows, as well as the speed at which the Copilot+ PC initiative rose and fell into obscurity, there's quite a lot at stake for Microsoft. You'll notice some familiar faces in the crowd already! I've been liveblogging alongside some of these folks for longer than I'd like to admit. We've made it inside, and are seating in some rather cramped seats. Good news is we are in the second row so we will have a good view. (Shoutouts to "Bob's uncle" and "dude" for their Big Surface Energy comments!) While they get settled, a new comment has appeared! User "Guest" said "Microsoft needs to streamline its windows, and focus on creating a bloatware free version" How many of you agree? And yes I'll bet some Windows news will be announced today. Right now're lined up and waiting to get in. I've never been to this area of SF along the waterfront, it's lovely! Karissa says they've arrived at the event and are in line to get in! Let's be clear, the news you're referring to is the pricing of the Xreal Aura Android XR glasses that were introduced at Google I/O this year, right? They'll cost $1,279. Or, in less understandable but more painful terms, an arm and half a leg. At least we don't think Microsoft is going to show off any smart glasses today? I give it 6 months before Google forgets about Googlebooks. Look at how its premiere Android XR partner (the Xreal Aura) just dumped its news out today. What's next, Geminibook? Oh lord now that I've said it... Anyway, Microsoft has at least kept the Surface branding consistent. While we wait, why don't I catch you up on recent developments in the broader laptop ecosystem. There has been a lot of interesting reports lately around a potential MacBook Ultra with an OLED touch screen and a Dynamic Island. If the rumor mill is to be trusted, it sounds like this could launch at the end of October. Meanwhile, Google recently launched its new AI-forward laptops called Googlebooks . If you're keeping track, the company has probably exhausted the laptop brands it can claim now, what with Pixelbook, Chromebook and Googlebook all having been used. I believe Devindra and Karissa are both making their way to the event space and we should hear from them what it's like there soon. What do you all want to know about the on-the-ground experience? I always always always ask about snacks. I won't say agentic but... maybe tons about little minions doing AI work for you ;) Seriously, this is the hot topic now, so I'm sure that will be the bulk of the event. Maybe Microsoft will try to launch another big AI feature too, but its track record with that hasn't been great. Morning! It will be interesting to see how Microsoft justifies that kind of price if it does land somewhere in the $3,000 range (which I agree is likely given everything we know). I suspect a lot of it will hinge on what Dev said a little bit ago... it's for hardcore AI folks. I'd bet we will hear all about how great this laptop is for agentic coding, AI development etc. Devindra, aside from the Surface Laptop Ultra and... AI... What word do you think we'll hear most at this afternoon's keynote? And don't say "Agentic"... I hope we'll return to the days of great $999 laptops eventually! Welp TIL that's how much the MacBook Pro starts at! I am still in the mindset of ultraportable laptop pricing from 2016 I guess. But yes, I think this will cost a lot and I have to wonder who it's for. I'm not sure there's a massive market for $3,000 laptops in this economy. Whatever the case, the Surface Laptop Ultra definitely won't be for most consumers. And I think that will hold true for most of the RTX Spark systems. NVIDIA wants a slightly cheaper version of its DGX Spark tech for laptops and smaller desktops, but all AI hardware will need a ton of RAM to hold large models. A MacBook Pro 16-inch with 64GB of RAM starts at $4,000. RTX Spark systems can go up to 128G of RAM. Oh I'd put it more in the range of the MacBook Pro 16-inch, since it's a similar market they're going for. That thing starts at $2,999! stories.title: Expanding the Cyber Verification Program
stories.summary: We’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program (CVP), which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals.

sources.name: Anthropic
sources.title: Expanding the Cyber Verification Program
sources.text: We’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program (CVP), which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals. The program now consists of three access tiers, which allow security teams to apply for the level of access that best suits their work. Each tier includes access to our most capable models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and new models moving forward. Interested customers can apply here . Cybersecurity is inherently dual use: the same capabilities that enable a security team to find and fix a vulnerability can also help a malicious actor exploit it. For this reason, our generally available models, such as Claude Opus 5.5 , Claude Fable 5.1 , and Claude Sonnet 5.5 , have conservative cyber safeguards that block most cyber work. This is intended to limit the harmful activities malicious actors can carry out using our models, while we continue to work to reduce false positives for secure coding. But defenders also need access to the best tools and most powerful capabilities to secure their systems. For the past six months, we’ve enabled trusted access through two programs: Project Glasswing and the CVP . The former gave a group of organizations securing the most critical software access to Claude Mythos; the latter gave vetted security teams access to reduced safeguards on Claude Opus and Claude Sonnet models. Now, we’re integrating these programs into one expanded offering, designed to give more security organizations access to the capabilities they need to protect their systems. The updated access tiers make specific model capabilities available to security professionals based on the scope of their cyber work. Each has different verification requirements and security controls. Defense Access is for defensive work, including security operations center and incident response tasks, reverse-engineering malware, and analyzing and validating vulnerabilities. Examples of qualifying organizations include security teams at companies, nonprofits, universities, and government bodies who are defending systems they own or maintain; operators of critical infrastructure of any size, such as regional hospitals or municipal utilities; smaller security firms; open-source maintainers; and individual researchers with a track record of reported vulnerabilities. We expect many organizations conducting defensive cybersecurity work to qualify for this tier. We aim to respond to applications within a few days. Red Team Access adds authorized penetration testing and red-teaming to the defensive uses above. Examples of qualifying organizations include in-house red teams, government red teams, and security and penetration testing firms. Organizations in this tier can only perform adversarial testing against systems they are authorized to test, including IT systems in critical industries. Users will still experience real-time blocks on actions that could cause physical harm or mass disruption, such as deploying ransomware, damaging physical systems, or pen testing high-risk safety systems. Given the increased eligibility requirements and security controls, we expect applications in this tier to take a few weeks to review. Qualifying organizations will be enrolled in the Defense Access tier while we review their Red Team Access applications. Currently, this tier is for organizations only; individual researchers are not eligible. Specialized Access , which has the fewest cyber blocks, is reserved for a limited set of verified organizations that are authorized to test safety systems that could impact people’s lives or disrupt markets, such as flight operating systems, power grids, telecom networks, interbank transfer infrastructure, and government administrative networks. For this tier, we currently review every organization in depth in collaboration with the US government. Existing members of Project Glasswing will transition to this tier and do not require reapproval for current models. Our generally available models can continue to be used for tasks such as code review, patching known issues, vulnerability finding in owned source code, and triage of security alerts. Data retention is required for organizations enrolled in the program so that we can monitor for cyber misuse. Once Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS)—a new solution that combines the privacy of zero data retention with robust safeguards—is available later this fall, eligible organizations will be able to store data in cloud infrastructure they control. Until EFS is available, organizations with access to Claude Fable 5.1 or Claude Mythos 5.1 with zero data retention can also use CVP with zero data retention. To register interest in EFS, fill out this form . Because this evaluation involves complex, interactive offensive scenarios, we would expect Claude to experience significant blocks both on the generally available model and in the Defense Access tier, while experiencing no blocks in the Red Team Access and Specialized Access tiers. We will continue to refine our tier-based classifiers over time. sources.title: Anthropic folds Project Glasswing into an expanded three-tier Cyber Verification Program
sources.text: Anthropic PBC today expanded its Cyber Verification Program into three tiers of access for vetted security teams, with fewer blocks on cybersecurity work at each step up. The overhaul is aimed at a restriction Anthropic built into its own products. Because the company treats cybersecurity as dual-use, its generally available models carry conservative classifiers that block most cyber work. When Claude Opus 5.5 launched Sept. 22 , most security tasks sent to it were routed to the older Opus 4.8. Anthropic is folding Project Glasswing into the program at the same time. Since April , Glasswing has given Claude Mythos access to organizations that secure critical software, and Anthropic widened it to 150 more organizations in June . Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are available at every tier of the new structure, and later models will be added as they ship. Defense Access is the entry tier, meant for defensive jobs such as incident response and malware reverse engineering. Security teams defending systems they own or maintain qualify, whether they work for a company, a university or a government body. Individual researchers with a record of reported vulnerabilities can apply too, as can critical infrastructure operators as small as a regional hospital. Anthropic expects many organizations doing defensive work to qualify and is aiming to respond to applications within a few days. Red Team Access opens up authorized penetration testing and red-teaming against systems an organization has permission to test. Even at this level, Anthropic’s classifiers block requests in real time when the work moves toward something like deploying ransomware. Applicants wait a few weeks for a review and sit in the Defense Access tier in the meantime, and individual researchers are shut out of the tier for now. Specialized Access carries the fewest cyber blocks of the three. Only organizations cleared to test safety systems like power grids and telecom networks qualify, since failures there could put lives at risk or disrupt markets. Anthropic vets each of them in depth with the U.S. government, and existing Glasswing members move straight into the tier without reapproval for current models. Enrolled organizations must allow data retention so Anthropic can watch for misuse. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards , due later this year, will let eligible customers keep that data in cloud infrastructure they control. Anthropic tested the tiers on the multistage cyber operations benchmark CyScenarioBench, with Claude Opus 5.5 running each of its 10 challenges five times. Every attempt without program access was blocked on the first prompt. Because the scenarios are offensive, Anthropic had expected heavy blocking in the Defense Access tier, where 46 of the 50 runs were stopped at some point. At the Red Team level nothing was blocked and the model finished 34 of its 50 runs. Anthropic said that result is effectively the same as the model’s 67.6% success rate with no safeguards applied. Outside the lab, the argument for widening access comes from the Mythos program the new structure absorbs. Partners in Project Glasswing found at least 129,000 verified vulnerabilities between April and July, and Anthropic’s own scanning of open-source code turned up 5,500 more through October. Of that combined total, more than 33,000 have been rated critical or high severity. The figures draw on just 33 partner reports, and the company said the true impact is likely at least five times higher. Fewer than half of the partners disclosed patch counts, often because fixes were still underway. The program is available through the Claude Platform, Google LLC’s Vertex AI and Microsoft Corp.’s Foundry service.
